Sidonie-Gabrielle Colette (28 January 1873 – 3 August 1954), known mononymously as Colette or as Colette Willy, was a French author and woman of letters. She was also a mime, actress, and journalist. Colette is best known in the English-speaking world for her 1944 novella Gigi, which was the basis for the 1958 film and the 1973 stage production of the same name. Her short story collection The Tendrils of the Vine is also famous in France.
Le Horla was originally published in 1887

In the early 1900s, she wrote the enormously successful Claudine novels, but they were published under the pen name of her husband, Henry Gauthier-Villars, better known as
"Willy." He already ran what was essentially a writing factory, employing ghostwriters whose work appeared under his name. Colette's books made "Willy" famous and became a commercial phenomenon, while her name was absent from the covers.
